newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 22.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
PUNJAB'S FIRST WOMAN CHIEF MINISTER SWORN IN

Rajinder Kaur Bhattal was sworn in as the first woman chief minister of Punjab, replacing Harcharan Singh Brar. She is the third chief minister the state has had during the tenure of the present assembly. Bhattal's appointment followed Brar's resignation from chief ministership yesterday which the state governor accepted. The Congress, to which Bhattal belongs, has allowed an all women team to lead the party in Punjab. All India Congress Committee joint secretary Ambika Soni has been asked to continue supervising the affairs of the party.
The Times Of India
MISS WORLD ORGANISERS APPEAL AGAINST COURT RESTRICTIONS

Organisers of the Miss World 1996 pageant, Amitabh Bachchan Corporation (ABCL), appealed against the Karnataka High Court order that it be held under judicial scrutiny. The case will be heard by the Supreme Court. Appealing against the court's ruling, ABCL said the restrictions would cause problems in holding a free and open competition. On a public interest petition by some anti-pageant women's organisations, the state high court had issued directives to ensure the show did not encourage obscenity. The court also restrained the Karnataka government from deploying para-military forces for the event.
The Economic Times
GORDON WU TO CHANGE POWER PROJECT SITE

Gordon Wu's Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) decided to change the site of its proposed 10,560-megawatt power project in Orissa. Sources said the project would be shifted from Hirma to a site in the Gopalpur area in the state. Sources said the new site was closer to the pit head at Ib Valley and therefore the company could save on transportation cost. Also, in the new area, there would be fewer displacement of people since most of the land was owned by the government, sources added.
INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK LOGS TWO PCT RISE IN NET

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) recorded two percent growth in net profit for the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). IDBI's net profit rose to 5.14 billion rupees from 5.03 billion rupees in the first half of 1995/96. While the operating income of IDBI rose by 18 percent from 23.57 billion rupees to 27.76 billion rupees, the institution's expenditure shot up by 23 percent from 17.27 billion rupees to 21.23 billion rupees.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS PLAN JOINT DIVESTMENT

The inter-institutional committee has recommended joint divestment of shares held by financial institutions (FIs) in companies showing poor returns. This will apply in cases of bad performance, unethical practice by management, dissensions among promoters or major shareholders and defaults on repayment of FI debt by companies. Joint divestment will also be considered in companies not paying dividend, sick units and companies where the management is prosecuted by investigating agencies. The report, if accepted, will have a direct bearing on companies such as Modi Rubber and ITC Ltd. At Modi Rubber, promoters and FIs have been at loggerheads while the ITC management was prosecuted.
INDIAN TOBACCO MAJOR AT WAR WITH B.A.T

ITC chairman Yogi Deveshwar is reportedly planning to wage a war with its British partner B.A.T to ward off any attempts by the latter to get control of the company. B.A.T already has a 32 percent stake in ITC. According to ITC sources, Norman Davis, former B.A.T nominee on ITC's board, had earlier promised to Deveshwar that B.A.T would pay off the Chitalias the amount ITC owed to the latter and help Deveshwar stay on as ITC chairman if he fulfilled some conditions. These included Deveshwar helping B.A.T to acquire 51 percent stake in ITC and allowing a B.A.T nominee to be the executive director of ITC's tobacco division. Deveshwar apparently refused to fall in line.
Financial Express
LARSON AND TOUBRO, ALUMINIUM PECHINEY TO TIE UP

Global aluminium giant Aluminium Pechiney of France is likely to be the new foreign collaborator of Indian engineering major Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) in the latter's proposed one million tonne alumina project in Orissa. L&T sources said the talks were at an advanced stage. The company is also in talks with other international majors like Kaizer. Earlier, L&T had signed a pact with U.S.-based primary metal manufacturer Alcoa for technological tie-up and equity participation in the 100 percent export oriented alumina project. But the talks failed as Alcoa insisted on coming up with the plant by 2002.
TATA TEA NET PROFIT RISES

Tata Tea reported a 25 percent rise in net profit to 353 million rupees for the half-year ended September, 1996. The company had a net profit of 283.1 million rupees in the same period of last year. The company's margins, however, appeared strained because of stagnant other income and rising finance costs. While income from operations surged 40 percent to 3.15 billion rupees from 2.24 billion rupees in the earlier period, other income declined to 107.8 million rupees from 113 million rupees previously.
EXPORTS DECLINE SHARPLY

The fall in exports during April-September 1996 and slowdown in the industrial sphere could affect the economy as a whole. The Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) said there was a 9.8 percent increase in exports in dollar terms during the said period. The FIFO said introduction of a minimum alternate tax, lack of credit, and conflict in policies of the finance and commerce ministries were reasons behind the slowdown. According to the FIFO, export of leather products declined by over 11 percent, while garments exports rose by a mere 0.6 percent. However, engineering goods showed an eight percent hike in exports.
SLUMP IN CAPITAL MARKET HITS MERCHANT BANKERS

About 40 merchant bankers have asked the bourse regulator (SEBI) for downgradation. Over a dozen merchant bankers have not applied for renewal of their licences. The reason for many merchant bankers seeking downgradation is their failure to meet the net worth requirement due to a slump in the capital market. The merchant bankers had failed to get much business with the number of public issues falling sharply. According to sources, companies raised only 140 billion rupees from the capital market in fiscal 1995/96 (April-March) against 381.82 billion rupees in 1994/95. In the first six months of 1996/97, only 44 billion rupees were raised from the primary market.
U.S. WEST OFFERS TECHNOLOGY PACKAGE TO BPL CELLULAR The

American multinational U.S. West offered a total technology package to BPL Cellular Holdings, replacing all other foreign collaborators. Sources said the development had come as an image boost for the TPG Nambiar-led company on the eve of its $200 million American Depository Receipt issue. The American company's offer would help BPL Cellular Holdings weather the shock that could have been created by the exit of its three other collaborators - France Telecom, Telecom Denmark and LCC Investments of the UK.
Business Standard
FAILURE TO HIKE PETRO PRICES TO HIT STATE OIL COMPANIES

Public sector (PSU) refineries are evaluating options to meet working capital needs in the wake of the government's failure to rise the petro-prices. The United Front panel's stand against the hike has dashed their hopes for realisation of their long-pending dues from the Oil Coordination Committee. The decision is likely to affect the oil companies' plans to raise money from the capital markets. The Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd has postponed its public issue. The divestment plans for Indian Oil Corporation may also be hit. This may also affect the government's budgeted revenue from its disinvestment plans in the oil PSUs.
The Observer
FIFTH PAY COMMISSION ASKED TO DEFER REPORT

The finance ministry unofficially instructed the Fifth Pay Commission not to submit its report before February 1997 in a bid to contain fiscal deficit within the budgeted target. By delaying the commission's report, the government can save as much as 27 billion rupees on the non-Plan expenditure front in the current Government sources said the Commission now also had a legitimate reason to delay its report. In the wake of the recent postal and telecommunication strike on the bonus issue, the government asked the Commission to additionally review the bonus policy and suggest measures for the future.
Business Line
STOCK WATCH SYSTEM IN OFFING

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the stock market regulator, is planning a sophisticated Stock Watch System similar to those in developed markets. The Stock Watch System would detect abuses such as market manipulation and insider trading. Meanwhile, the regulator has asked all stock exchanges to maintain a weekly cap of 25 percent in the band for scrips that are traded above par in order to check abnormal price variations of traded scrips.
